messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: perf.cliff.continuous_batch detected for service=runtime-region-us-west-2 at 2734567890. 95th latency spike -> +420ms; kv_cache_evictions spiked. Pager: @maria (oncall) :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): seen it, acking. oncall taking lead. grabbing quick metrics + recent deploys.

jordan (sre): +1, pulling traces. early signal looks like sustained queue depth growth on shard-3 -> continuous batching heartbeat oscillation + microbatch size blowups. kv cache thrash follows.

maria (oncall): timeline? any recent config pushes?

jordan (sre): no infra deploys in last 30m. there was a model change rollout to /catalog/redwood/opt-13b at 2720000000 but that was gradual. suspect workload change (burst from a single tenant).

claudia (infra): checking node headroom and autoscaler. current pool at 72% GPU util on west-2; autoscale didn't trigger because we hit queue caps earlier.

ryan (platform): if queue cap hits, cb heartbeat can start oscillating — workers flush KV too frequently which forces cache invalidations. can we temporarily lower `cb.heartbeat_ms` and cap microbatch size?

maria (oncall): propose immediate mitigations:
1) reduce cb.heartbeat_ms from 200 -> 80 (runtime config)
2) set cb.max_microbatch = 4 (was 16)
3) increase per-shard queue limit by +20% to avoid backpressure hard clamp
4) enable per-tenant short-circuit for heavy prefixes (disable prefix caching for offending tenant)

jordan (sre): agree. I'll push the runtime flags as a hotfix on a small subset of pods first. apply to shard-0..2, observe 10m, then roll.

ryan (platform): commands to flip (use control-plane API):
```bash
# reduce heartbeat and microbatch cap
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/configs -d '{"key":"cb.heartbeat_ms","value":"80"}'
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/configs -d '{"key":"cb.max_microbatch","value":"4"}'
# scale per-shard queue threshold
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/scale -d '{"shard":"all","queue_increase_pct":20}'
```

claudia (infra): I'll pre-warm 2 additional nodes as a safety net. adding capacity now. ETA ~4m.

jordan (sre): patch applied to shards 0-2. initial metrics: 95th latency down ~170ms, kv_cache_evictions rate halved. continuing roll to rest of shards.

maria (oncall): what's customer impact? any 5xx or user-facing errors?

ops-liaison: acme-corp (tenant id: acme-42) reported intermittent 503s during window 2734567700-2734567860. also elevated tail latency for 2 other customers. have them flagged.

emma (product): we should notify affected customers after stabilization. prepare a short status note: root cause = transient cache eviction cascade caused by high-concurrency microbatch blowups; mitigation in progress.

jordan (sre): rolling to remaining shards. metrics look stable after full rollout: 95th back to baseline +40ms, kv_evictions trending down. no new 503s observed in last 3m.

maria (oncall): good. log runbook steps for postmortem. immediate followups:
- create incident ticket (INC-2734567890) with timeline and exact config diffs
- collect heap/KV snapshots for affected shards
- correlate tenant traffic spikes + prompt patterns

ryan (platform): one more note: the underlying cause seems to be an interaction between `cb.max_microbatch` and the adaptive `kb_prefetch` logic that makes microbatches jump when queue latency spikes — that made heartbeat thrash. long-term fix: add smoothing to microbatch growth and a hard upper bound at the runtime kernel level.

claudia (infra): nodes pre-warmed and autoscaler adjusted to be slightly more aggressive for next 30m.

ops-liaison: customer comms: drafting now, will post to status.redwood.com + direct emails to affected accounts.

maria (oncall): handing off to jordan for overnight stabilization and postmortem kickoff. jordan — you're primary for the follow-up. i'll update incident channel + set SLA check. thanks team. :white_check_mark:

jordan (sre): taking handoff. I'll run the KV integrity sweep and add guardrails to the runtime flags so future rollouts don't leave `cb.max_microbatch` high under queue stress.

emma (product): add impacted customers list to the incident ticket and include recommended customer-facing language.

maria (oncall): final notes for handoff -> severity: sev-2, duration window: 2734567700-2734567960, customer impact: intermittent 503s for acme-corp + elevated tail latency for 2 midsize tenants, mitigation: runtime flags + small scale up. next steps: postmortem scheduled, assign owners for long-term fix.

jordan (sre): leaving a small dashboard link with key charts -> https://grafana.internal/d/CB/continuous-batch-heartbeat?orgId=1&from=2734567600&to=2734568050

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. paging cleared. closing pager in 10.

incident-bot: Pager cleared by maria (oncall) at 2734568060.
